title: UN Transparency Protocol (UNTP)
authority: UN/CEFACT — United Nations Economic Commission for Europe
usedFor: Product-transparency and conformity credential detail. The nearest community profile to this project's credential work, and the only Layer-2 entry with a directly consumable artefact.
licence: CC BY 4.0 for UNTP itself — confirmed 2026-08-11 from the current canonical spec site's own footer (`https://untp.unece.org/`, `.../docs/specification/DigitalProductPassport/`), stated verbatim: "All UN/CEFACT standards are free to use under CC By 4.0 license", elaborated in the FAQ: "provided free of charge for use by anyone... any party may modify the UNTP for their own purposes... licensed for unrestricted public use." Real tension, not fully resolved: the same site's generic `/terms` page, and the host actually serving the JSON-LD context (`vocabulary.uncefact.org`), both carry only a bare copyright notice with no licence grant at all. CC BY 4.0 is the more specific, on-topic, repeated statement; the ambiguity is between two of UN/CEFACT's own pages, not a survey error.
source: https://untp.unece.org/ and its FAQ/specification pages, cross-checked against the context host `vocabulary.uncefact.org/untp/0.7.0/context/` — fetched directly.
finding: `ProductIDGranularity` (Model/Batch/Item, exposed via `idGranularity` + typed `modelNumber`/`batchNumber`/`itemNumber` companion fields on the DPP's `Product` class) is not merely similar to `RegistrationGranularity` — it is the **same three-level axis**, isomorphic. UNTP's typed companion-field pattern is more structured than `RegistrationRequest` currently is, worth a look independent of any IRI decision. The Digital Conformity Credential shape (`ConformityAttestation`: assessor/assessment level, attestation type, reference scheme/profile, `conformityAssessment[]` with criteria/performance/conformance, subject via assessed product/facility/organisation) is real prior art for something `dpp-vc` does not have at all today — `dpp-vc/src/credential/types.rs` currently defines no conformity credential type, only access/status credentials. Version is still pre-1.0; UNTP's own specification page states 1.0 is targeted for 1 September 2026, a few weeks out.
nextStep: Map, selectively, once 1.0 ships — not now. Don't wire a pre-1.0 remote `@context` as an operational dependency; this project already removed two remote contexts for 404ing. Before then: read the `ConformityAttestation` shape as design input for a conformity credential type, and compare the `idGranularity`+companion-fields pattern against `RegistrationRequest` independent of the IRI question. Resolve the `/terms`-vs-footer licence tension by asking UNECE directly before citing the CC-BY-4.0 grant in anything published, rather than picking the convenient reading.
